SuSiEOut

SuSiEOut implements SuSiE-OUT, a sparse summary-statistic fine-mapping method for loci where a causal variant may have been omitted from the tested set, for example by a minor allele frequency or SNP-only filter. Each single effect can be null, assigned to a tested variant, or assigned to an omitted variant (an OUT state). An omitted variant is represented by its linkage disequilibrium (LD) fingerprint: its LD with the tested variants, taken from a sequencing reference panel that contains it.

In the code, arguments and fields named examined_* refer to tested variants, and excluded_* or outside_* refer to omitted variants.

Full documentation, with a reference page for every function, is at https://weinstocklab.github.io/SuSiEOut/.

Acknowledgements

SuSiE-OUT builds on the Sum of Single Effects (SuSiE) model of Wang, Sarkar, Carbonetto and Stephens (2020) and its summary-statistic extension SuSiE-RSS (Zou, Carbonetto, Wang and Stephens, 2022), and uses susieR as a reference implementation. We are grateful to the SuSiE authors for making their methods and software openly available. SuSiEOut is an independent project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by the SuSiE authors or the susieR maintainers.

Installation 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("weinstocklab/SuSiEOut")

Example 

library(SuSiEOut)
locus <- susieout_simulate_locus(1, architecture = "entirely_omitted")
fit <- susieout_fit(
    locus$z, locus$n, locus$R_analysis, locus$wgs_ld,
    locus$examined_ids, effect_prior = "robust_mixture", L = 10,
    count_prior = susieout_count_prior(lambda_total = 1,
                                       out_fraction = 0.10))
summary(fit)
susieout_credible_sets(fit)

The dense nuisance parameter is total local infinitesimal variance, not the coefficient placed directly on the z-score covariance. For p tested variants and GWAS size n, infinitesimal_variance = h2_dense fits

R + (n * h2_dense / p) R^2 + omega I.

This scaling lets the same local architecture be compared coherently across GWAS sample sizes. Fixed fits report both local_h2 and the resulting covariance_multiplier; fixed variance fractions are not labeled posterior probabilities.

The count prior is specified at the locus level. Changing L changes the numerical approximation but not the prior probability that the locus contains any sparse effect. lambda_total controls sparse-effect count and out_fraction controls how that count is divided between tested variants and omitted variants (OUT states).

Heterogeneous banks should not impose one sparse count or one positive dense variance on every locus. Spike-and-grid averaging combines sparse-count and nuisance states using a comparable variational evidence. Here training_loci is a bank of loci with known causal variants, such as those from susieout_simulate_locus(); see ?susieout_train_prior for the required format:

sparse_prior <- susieout_train_prior(training_loci, em_iterations = 0)
nuisance_prior <- susieout_train_nuisance_grid(
    training_loci, sparse_prior,
    infinitesimal_grid = c(0, 0.002, 0.008, 0.032),
    ld_mismatch_grid = c(0, 0.04, 0.12))
prior_grid <- susieout_prior_grid()
fit <- susieout_fit_grid(
    locus$z, locus$n, locus$R_analysis, locus$wgs_ld,
    locus$examined_ids, trained_prior = sparse_prior,
    prior_grid = prior_grid, nuisance_prior = nuisance_prior)

susieout_train_prior(..., em_update = "nuisance_only") provides a global EM diagnostic without feeding fitted OUT responsibilities back into the count prior. A zero out_fraction fits a model that assumes no causal variant was omitted and needs no LD fingerprints.

For large loci, R_analysis may be a Matrix sparse matrix. The sparse backend avoids forming the full tested-by-tested LD matrix in dense form and supports the R + dI nuisance covariance (infinitesimal_variance = 0).
